\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{فکر} \ur{کرنا} (fikr karnā)}{فکر کرنا (fikr karnā)}]{\ur{فکر} \ur{کرنا} (fikr karnā) — to worry}

\label{lesson:UR-C446-fikr-karna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to crouch out of sight, then the Urdu for to huddle.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{فکر} \ur{کرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{فکر} \ur{کرنا}} — \emph{fikr karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to worry\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{امی} \ur{ہر} \ur{بات} \ur{کی} \ur{فکر} \ur{کرتی} \ur{ہیں۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ammī har bāt kī fikr kartī haiṅ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Mum worries about everything.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{بچوں} \ur{کی} \ur{فکر} \ur{کی}, \emph{us ne bachchoṅ kī fikr kī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{فکر} \ur{کرنا}} (\emph{fikr karnā}) is built from \textbf{\ur{فکر}}, usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{fikr}, \textquotedblleft{}thought\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ur{کرنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}: in Urdu the thought has become a worry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fikr karnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fikr karnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ammī har bāt kī fikr kartī haiṅ.} — Mum worries about everything.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to crouch out of sight, then the Urdu for to huddle, then say \emph{fikr karnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{فکر} \ur{کرنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To worry\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{تشویش} (tashvīsh)}{تشویش (tashvīsh)}]{\ur{تشویش} (tashvīsh) — anxiety; concern}

\label{lesson:UR-C446-tashvish}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to huddle, then the Urdu for to worry.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{تشویش}}
\textbf{\ur{تشویش}} — \emph{tashvīsh} — \textquotedblleft{}anxiety; concern\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بچے} \ur{کے} \ur{بخار} \ur{پر} \ur{ماں} \ur{کو} \ur{تشویش} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bachche ke bukhār par māṅ ko tashvīsh hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The mother is anxious about the child's fever.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{تشویش}} (\emph{tashvīsh}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{tashwīsh}, \textquotedblleft{}a stirring up, a disturbance\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بوجھ} (bojh)}{بوجھ (bojh)}]{\ur{بوجھ} (bojh) — a burden; a load}

\label{lesson:UR-C446-bojh}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to worry, then the Urdu for anxiety.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بوجھ}}
\textbf{\ur{بوجھ}} — \emph{bojh} — \textquotedblleft{}a burden; a load\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{قرض} \ur{کا} \ur{بوجھ} \ur{اس} \ur{کے} \ur{دل} \ur{پر} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{qarz kā bojh us ke dil par hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The burden of the debt weighs on his mind.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بوجھ}} (\emph{bojh}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{vahyá}, \textquotedblleft{}something to be carried\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 11465).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{تڑپنا} (taṛapnā)}{تڑپنا (taṛapnā)}]{\ur{تڑپنا} (taṛapnā) — to writhe; to be in anguish}

\label{lesson:UR-C446-tarapna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for anxiety, then the Urdu for a burden.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{تڑپنا}}
\textbf{\ur{تڑپنا}} — \emph{taṛapnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to writhe; to be in anguish\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{پرندہ} \ur{زمین} \ur{پر} \ur{تڑپ} \ur{رہا} \ur{تھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{parindā zamīn par taṛap rahā thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The bird was writhing on the ground.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \ur{وہ} \ur{درد} \ur{سے} \ur{تڑپا}, \emph{voh dard se taṛpā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{تڑپنا}} (\emph{taṛapnā}) is inherited from \emph{taḍapphaḍ}, \textquotedblleft{}agitate\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs (CDIAL 5634).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{دھڑکنا} (dhaṛaknā)}{دھڑکنا (dhaṛaknā)}]{\ur{دھڑکنا} (dhaṛaknā) — to throb; to pound (of the heart)}

\label{lesson:UR-C446-dharakna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a burden, then the Urdu for to writhe.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{دھڑکنا}}
\textbf{\ur{دھڑکنا}} — \emph{dhaṛaknā} — \textquotedblleft{}to throb; to pound (of the heart)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{امتحان} \ur{سے} \ur{پہلے} \ur{میرا} \ur{دل} \ur{دھڑک} \ur{رہا} \ur{تھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{imtihān se pehle merā dil dhaṛak rahā thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Before the exam my heart was pounding.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{دل} \ur{دھڑکا}, \emph{voh dil dhaṛkā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{دھڑکنا}} (\emph{dhaṛaknā}) is inherited from \emph{dhaḍ}, \textquotedblleft{}throb, beat\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs (CDIAL 6711); \textbf{\ur{دھڑکن}}, \textquotedblleft{}a heartbeat\textquotedblright{}, is its noun.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}
